name: node
one_liner: The core program that runs JavaScript outside a web browser — the engine behind huge amounts of backend software and developer tooling.
buyer: Not a product for an end buyer; it's foundational open-source infrastructure used by every company running a JavaScript backend, maintained under the OpenJS Foundation.
business_use_cases: A hosting or cloud provider markets fast Node.js runtime support and version upgrades as part of its platform offering.
A consultancy offers paid 'upgrade my app to the latest LTS Node.js' migration services to companies stuck on end-of-life versions.
A performance consultancy sells profiling and optimization audits for companies running high-traffic Node.js backends.

money_ideas.idea: Sell Node.js version-upgrade and migration services to companies on deprecated or unsupported releases.
Offer ongoing performance-tuning retainers for companies running Node.js at scale.

steal_this: There's no weekend product in the runtime itself — the real opportunity is a service business: offer fixed-price Node.js LTS upgrade packages to companies you find still running old versions.
